cars.chooseCar: Please choose the car from the account.
cars.delayHint: The values come from the car's manufacturer and are at least 15 minutes old.

cars.guideStep1: Open the EU Data Act portal and log in with your brand account (the same email and password as in the brand's app):
cars.guideStep2: Confirm the consent to the data transfer.
cars.guideStep3: Link your car to the account if it is not listed there yet.
cars.guideStep4: Start a continuous data request with data every 15 minutes. Without it the portal delivers nothing.
cars.guideTitle: Once in a browser: set up the portal
cars.guideWait: It can take a few hours until the first data arrives in the portal. Until then OpenAmpere keeps asking by itself.
cars.intro: OpenAmpere can fetch your car's state of charge, range and odometer from its manufacturer. For cars from Volkswagen, Audi, Škoda, SEAT and CUPRA this works through the Volkswagen group's EU Data Act portal, with your brand account. The values arrive about every 15 minutes and are at least 15 minutes old.
cars.loadVehicles: Load the cars of the account
cars.loginToChange: Please log in to set up or change the cars.
cars.name: Name
cars.noFreeWallbox: OpenAmpere counts the charges at a wallbox it controls itself (More → Connection → Wallbox). Without one you only see state of charge, range and odometer.
cars.noWallboxHint: Add a wallbox OpenAmpere controls itself, then it counts the charges of this car.
cars.passwordLost: The stored password could not be read, for example after restoring a backup on another device. Please enter it again under “Change”.
cars.readOnlyHint: OpenAmpere only reads. It sends nothing to the car, and the wallbox control does not follow these values. OpenAmpere stores your password encrypted because the portal has no lasting login.
cars.removeHint: OpenAmpere forgets the login, the stored values and the charges of this car. Nothing changes in the portal or at the manufacturer.
cars.setupMissing: A step in the portal is still missing

cars.unofficialHint: The portal is not an official interface for apps. If the manufacturer changes the login, fetching can fail until OpenAmpere is adapted. OpenAmpere is not part of the Volkswagen group.
cars.vehicleChosen: The car with the VIN ending …{end} is chosen. Load the cars of the account to choose another one.
cars.waitingFirstData: Waiting for the first data from the portal
cars.wallboxHint: A wallbox OpenAmpere controls itself. While the car is plugged in there, it shows the state of charge, and every charge is stored with state of charge and odometer.

minSoc.hint: Up to this state of charge, the car charges right away, also from the grid. After that, the charging mode applies. This way there is always enough in the battery for a short trip.

nativeWallbox.intro: OpenAmpere reads these wallboxes itself and can let them charge with your solar surplus, without evcc and without a cloud. You can set up several wallboxes.
nativeWallbox.name: Name
nativeWallbox.keyIntro: The wallbox talks encrypted in the home network. For this OpenAmpere needs its “local key”, a key of 16 characters. You fetch it once from the Tuya developer platform; after that OpenAmpere needs no cloud.
nativeWallbox.search: Search the home network for a Tuya wallbox
nativeWallbox.nothingFound: No Tuya wallbox found. Is it plugged in and connected to the Wi-Fi? You can also copy the IP address from your router.
nativeWallbox.noSearchInApp: In the Home Assistant app, OpenAmpere cannot search the home network. Please copy the IP address from your router.
nativeWallbox.addressHint: The IP address of the wallbox in your home network, e.g. {example}. Best give it the same address every time in your router.
nativeWallbox.localKeyHint: Exactly 16 characters, as they appear after “local_key”. Upper and lower case and special characters belong to it, quotation marks do not.
nativeWallbox.localKeySaved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
nativeWallbox.keyLostHint: OpenAmpere cannot read the stored local key of this wallbox, for example after a backup was restored on another computer. Until you enter it again, OpenAmpere neither reads nor controls the wallbox. Its other settings are kept.
nativeWallbox.maxCurrentHint: OpenAmpere sets at most this much, e.g. 16 for a red 16 A socket. The wallbox also limits to the value from its app.
nativeWallbox.deviceIdHint: The device ID is in the device list of the Tuya platform; the search fills it in. With it OpenAmpere finds the wallbox again when the router gives it a new address.
nativeWallbox.testOk: Connected. The wallbox reports {phases} phases, set to {current} A (firmware {firmware}).
nativeWallbox.removeHint: If OpenAmpere controlled the wallbox, it first sets your own charging current back as soon as the wallbox can be reached.
nativeWallbox.hintManual: OpenAmpere only shows the wallbox and changes nothing. You control it in its app as usual.

hintPv.one: Charges with solar surplus only. When it is not enough, the wallbox goes on with the lowest step (the battery or the grid supply the rest) and pauses only when it stays like this for 1 minute.
hintPv.other: Charges with solar surplus only. When it is not enough, the wallbox goes on with the lowest step (the battery or the grid supply the rest) and pauses only when it stays like this for {count} minutes.

nativeWallbox.awayHint: A portable wallbox is often unplugged. OpenAmpere asks again from time to time and reconnects by itself as soon as it is on the Wi-Fi.
nativeWallbox.searchUnavailable: The search is not possible on this computer right now. Please copy the IP address from your router.
nativeWallbox.nameHint: What the wallbox is called in OpenAmpere, for example “Garage” or “Portable wallbox”.
nativeWallbox.keyHowTo: How to get the local key (step by step)
nativeWallbox.keyStep1: On a computer, create a free account on iot.tuya.com.
nativeWallbox.keyStep2: Under “Cloud → Development”, create a project (“Create Cloud Project”). As data center choose the one your app account is in, in Germany “Central Europe”.
nativeWallbox.keyStep3: Add the service “IoT Core” to the project. It is a free trial; it is enough for fetching the key once.
nativeWallbox.keyStep4: In the project, under “Devices → Link App Account”, show the QR code and scan it in the Tuya or Smart Life app under “Me” with the scan icon at the top. The wallbox then appears in the device list, with its device ID.
nativeWallbox.keyStep5: Under “Cloud → API Explorer”, query the device details (“Query Device Details”) with the wallbox's device ID. The answer has the key after “local_key”. Copy these 16 characters into the field “Local key” below.
nativeWallbox.keyChanges: If you pair the wallbox again in the app, the local key changes; then fetch it again the same way. Do not pass the key on: it lets anyone control the wallbox in the home network. The pages of the Tuya platform change often, the names may differ slightly.
nativeWallbox.testHint: “Check connection” reads the wallbox once with these details. Nothing is changed on it.
nativeWallbox.whichControlled: OpenAmpere shows this wallbox and controls it with your solar power, without evcc.
nativeWallbox.whichChecked: OpenAmpere cannot control this wallbox yet. The check only reads it and creates a report you can share. This helps to support it soon.
nativeWallbox.full: {max} wallboxes are set up already, no more are possible.
nativeWallbox.noCarHint: No car plugged in: OpenAmpere changes nothing on the wallbox. The chosen charging mode applies as soon as you plug in a car. If the wallbox then starts by itself and in Solar mode there is not enough solar power, OpenAmpere stops charging right away.
nativeWallbox.hintMinpv: Always charges with at least the lowest step, faster with sun, but at most with the charging current below.
nativeWallbox.hintNow: Charges right away with the charging current below. Sun, battery or grid supply it; the battery may discharge into the car.
nativeWallbox.modeCurrent: Highest charging current in this mode
nativeWallbox.stopAfterHint: When a cloud comes in “Solar” mode, the wallbox goes on with the lowest step for this long. The battery or the grid supply the rest. Longer means fewer interruptions, shorter means less power from the grid. 1 to 60 minutes.
nativeWallbox.awayHintModbus: OpenAmpere cannot reach the wallbox right now and asks again from time to time. On EKD systems this is usually caused by the previous smartbox: as long as it has power, it holds the connection to the wallbox, and OpenAmpere cannot read it. If OpenAmpere should show the wallbox, disconnect the smartbox from power. If you have no smartbox, check that the wallbox is switched on and whether evcc or another program reads it.
nativeWallbox.hintReadOnly: OpenAmpere only shows this wallbox and changes nothing on it. It charges as it is set in its own app.
nativeWallbox.whichShown: OpenAmpere shows this wallbox: whether a car is plugged in and with how much power it charges. OpenAmpere cannot control it yet, it goes on charging as it is set in its own app. You can try out the charging modes as a simulation: OpenAmpere then only works out what it would do. With “Check only” you create a report instead, which helps to control it soon.
nativeWallbox.readOnlyIntro: OpenAmpere only reads the wallbox and changes nothing on it. On EKD systems the previous smartbox must stay disconnected from power for this, otherwise it holds the connection to the wallbox. If evcc already reads the wallbox, do not add it here as well: it may allow only one connection.
nativeWallbox.portHint: Leave empty for the usual port {port}.
nativeWallbox.testOkReadOnly: Connected. The wallbox reports {phases} phases and charges with at most {current} A (firmware {firmware}).
nativeWallbox.simulationNotice: Only a simulation: OpenAmpere writes nothing to this wallbox. It keeps charging as it is set in its own app, for example as soon as you plug in a car. In the charging modes other than “Manual”, OpenAmpere only works out when and with which current it would charge, and writes that into the log as a simulation.

planCharging.one: OpenAmpere would now charge with {current} A on 1 phase, about {power}.
planCharging.other: OpenAmpere would now charge with {current} A on {count} phases, about {power}.

nativeWallbox.planWaiting: OpenAmpere would not charge yet: it waits to see whether the surplus stays.
nativeWallbox.planNoSurplus: OpenAmpere would not charge now: there is too little solar surplus.
nativeWallbox.planOff: OpenAmpere would not charge now: the charging mode is “Off”.
nativeWallbox.planFinished: OpenAmpere would not charge now: the car takes no more power, it is probably full.
nativeWallbox.planNoCar: OpenAmpere would not charge now: no car is plugged in.
nativeWallbox.planUnknown: OpenAmpere has not worked anything out yet. It does so as soon as it reads the wallbox again.
nativeWallbox.noCarHintSimulation: No car plugged in. The simulation works it out as soon as you plug in a car. The wallbox itself then charges as it is set in its own app.
nativeWallbox.simHintManual: OpenAmpere only shows the wallbox. Choose another charging mode to try out how OpenAmpere would control it. Nothing is written.
nativeWallbox.simHintOff: Simulation: OpenAmpere would stop charging and not start it again.

simHintPv.one: Simulation: OpenAmpere would charge with solar surplus only. If it is no longer enough, it would go on with the lowest step and only pause after 1 minute like that.
simHintPv.other: Simulation: OpenAmpere would charge with solar surplus only. If it is no longer enough, it would go on with the lowest step and only pause after {count} minutes like that.

nativeWallbox.simHintMinpv: Simulation: OpenAmpere would always charge with at least the lowest step, faster in the sun, but at most with the current below.
nativeWallbox.simHintNow: Simulation: OpenAmpere would charge right away with the current below.
nativeWallbox.maxCurrentHintSimulation: The most OpenAmpere would set in the simulation. The wallbox also limits to its own highest current.

ownDeviceCard.autoHint: Runs on solar surplus according to your settings.
ownDeviceCard.fullPowerHint: Runs at full power for 2 hours, also on grid power. Then back to automatic.
ownDeviceCard.offHint: Stays off until you switch back to Automatic.

planForm.hint: evcc then charges so the target is reached by that time, preferably with solar or cheap power.
planForm.title: Charge by a set time

sponsor.expired: The evcc sponsor token expired on {date}. If your wallbox needs a sponsor token, it no longer charges through evcc. Get a new one on {link} and enter it in evcc under Configuration → Sponsorship, or connect a wallbox OpenAmpere knows itself here under wallbox “direct”.
sponsor.expiresOn: The evcc sponsor token expires on {date}. Get a new one on {link} and enter it in evcc under Configuration → Sponsorship.
sponsor.expiresSoon: The evcc sponsor token expires soon. Get a new one on {link} and enter it in evcc under Configuration → Sponsorship.
sponsor.trial: evcc runs with the test token, which is valid for only a few days. If your wallbox needs a sponsor token, it will stop charging through evcc after that. More: {link}.
sponsor.trialExpired: The evcc test token expired on {date}. If your wallbox needs a sponsor token, it no longer charges through evcc. Enter a valid token in evcc under Configuration → Sponsorship, or connect a wallbox OpenAmpere knows itself here under wallbox “direct”. More: {link}.
sponsor.trialUntil: evcc runs with the test token, which is valid only until {date}. If your wallbox needs a sponsor token, it will stop charging through evcc after that. More: {link}.

surplusOrder.batteryHint: The battery is charged up to this state of charge. After that, the devices below it get the solar power.
surplusOrder.title: Who gets solar power first?

wallboxCard.testModeLogged: Test mode: only logged, not sent to evcc

wallboxDirect.addressHint: IP address of the wallbox in your home network, e.g. {example}, not the one of the inverter. You can find it in your router's device list.
wallboxDirect.appMode: Which control mode does the manufacturer's app show?
wallboxDirect.appModeHint: For FoxESS in the Fox Switch app. Only for the report; you do not have to change anything.
wallboxDirect.fallbackHint: The wallbox keeps charging at the fallback current when an energy manager controls it over Modbus and then fails.
wallboxDirect.invalidNumbers: Please enter port and device address as numbers.
wallboxDirect.nothingChanges: The check only reads. Nothing is changed on the wallbox, and you do not have to change anything first.
wallboxDirect.ocppAddress: Enter this address in the manufacturer's app as the OCPP server (OCPP 1.6J, no password). The wallbox usually appends its ID.
wallboxDirect.ocppConnected: The wallbox is connected. OpenAmpere is listening.
wallboxDirect.ocppIntro: Many wallboxes can connect to a server over OCPP. OpenAmpere accepts the connection, only listens and asks for the settings. It does not start or stop anything and changes no setting.
wallboxDirect.ocppSwitchBack: Done? Switch the wallbox back to its previous control mode in the manufacturer's app, then create the diagnostics report.
wallboxDirect.ocppWaiting: Waiting for the wallbox, {minutes} min left. Some wallboxes connect only after a few minutes.
wallboxDirect.ocppWarning: For this you switch the wallbox to OCPP in the manufacturer's app. While it is set like this, neither the manufacturer's app nor evcc controls it, and without a charging profile it charges without a limit. Switch it back after the check.
wallboxDirect.otherHint: For other wallboxes you can read any registers under "Read a device" and share the diagnostics report. This helps to support your wallbox later.
wallboxDirect.outcomeBusy: The wallbox refuses reading ("device busy"). It probably runs in a control mode that does not allow Modbus. You do not have to change anything: this result helps too, please share the report.
wallboxDirect.outcomeConnectionRefused: A device is reachable at this address but does not accept a Modbus connection (port {ports}). On EKD systems the usual reason is the previous Smartbox: as long as it is running, OpenAmpere cannot read the wallbox. Unplug it from power for the check and check again, then you can plug it back in. If that does not help, evcc or another program may be reading the wallbox, or another device is at this address.
wallboxDirect.outcomeConnectionsTaken: The wallbox does not accept a connection right now because another device is already reading it. On EKD systems this is usually the previous Smartbox: as long as it is running, OpenAmpere cannot read the wallbox. Unplug it from power for the check and check again, then you can plug it back in. If you have no Smartbox, evcc or another program is probably reading the wallbox.
wallboxDirect.outcomeNoAnswer: The wallbox accepts the connection but does not answer the request properly. On EKD systems the usual reason is the previous Smartbox: as long as it is running, OpenAmpere cannot read the wallbox. Unplug it from power for the check and check again, then you can plug it back in. If that does not help, evcc may be reading the wallbox, or the device address is wrong.
wallboxDirect.outcomeReadable: Found. The wallbox can be read in its current control mode.
wallboxDirect.outcomeRejected: The wallbox answers but does not know these registers. Maybe it is another model or firmware. Please share the report.
wallboxDirect.outcomeUnreachable: No device answers at this address (port {ports}). Please check the address, you find the wallbox in the device list of your router. It must be switched on and in your home network.
wallboxDirect.outcomeUnresolved: OpenAmpere cannot find the name {host} in your home network. Please enter the IP address of the wallbox instead. You find it in the device list of your router, where a FoxESS wallbox is usually called "EVC-…".
wallboxDirect.outcomeUnresolvedLocalInApp: Names ending in .local do not work in the Home Assistant app. Please enter the IP address of the wallbox instead. You find it in the device list of your router, where a FoxESS wallbox is usually called "EVC-…".
wallboxDirect.portHint: Leave empty: OpenAmpere tries this wallbox's usual ports (502 and 1502).
wallboxDirect.preview: Preview: OpenAmpere checks your wallbox read-only and creates a report. It cannot control it this way yet. That first needs reports from real devices showing that all values are right.
wallboxDirect.reportHint: Please create the diagnostics report now and share it. It contains the result of the check, but no card number and no meter readings. The serial number is shortened in it unless you explicitly include it in full in the diagnostics.
wallboxDirect.search: Search the home network for the wallbox
wallboxDirect.unitHint: Usually 1. For FoxESS it is shown in the Fox Switch app.
wallboxDirect.way: How should OpenAmpere talk to the wallbox?
wallboxDirect.wired: Is the wallbox wired to the inverter (the manufacturer's solar charging)?
wallboxDirect.wiredHint: According to FoxESS, its solar charging needs the inverter in self-use mode, without an export limit. An export limit or charging the battery from the grid in OpenAmpere can interfere with it.
wallboxDirect.workModeControlled: through the app or a card
wallboxDirect.showLiveHint: OpenAmpere can also show this wallbox permanently, read only. Address, port and unit ID are taken over from the check.

wallboxPage.addressHint: On the same computer {local}, otherwise e.g. {example}
wallboxPage.copyFailed: Copying didn't work. Please select the configuration below and copy it.
wallboxPage.directAccessOff: evcc needs direct access to OpenAmpere by IP address. Turn it on in Home Assistant under Settings → Apps → OpenAmpere → Network, then open this page again.
wallboxPage.evccCredit: evcc is developed by the evcc community and is MIT-licensed. For some devices, evcc requires a sponsorship. OpenAmpere only uses evcc's open interface and contains no code from evcc.
wallboxPage.installHint: Easiest with Docker on the same computer as OpenAmpere. You set up the wallbox and vehicle in evcc, see the {link}.
wallboxPage.intro: The wallbox is controlled by {link}, an independent open-source project for solar charging. You can then operate it under “Devices”.
wallboxPage.meterHint: Then evcc doesn't need its own connection to the inverter, which allows only a few. Copy the meter configuration and paste it into evcc (evcc.yaml or “user-defined device”).
wallboxPage.passwordHint: Only needed if evcc requires a login for changes.
wallboxPage.priorityHint: You choose who gets solar power first (battery, wallbox, immersion heater) under “Devices”. OpenAmpere passes the battery priority on to evcc.
wallboxPage.replaceHostPlaceholder: In the configuration, replace {placeholder} with the IP address of your Home Assistant.
wallboxPage.savedKeep: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
wallboxPage.sponsorHint: For many wallboxes evcc requires a sponsor token, which costs money. The {link} shows whether yours is one of them: "sponsor free" means no token. The evcc test token is valid for only a few days.
wallboxPage.title: Set up wallbox
